en: The Lotus Face Sūtra, Volume One, from the Mahāyāna Sūtra Piṭaka, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was dwelling on the bank of the Monkey Pond at Vaiśālī.
Within the multi-storied pavilion, the Tathāgata will soon relinquish his life-span.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda:
"I shall now go with you to the city of Pāpā; there is an elder named Viśvāmitra whom I wish to convert."
Ānanda said, "So be it!
I shall receive the Tathāgata’s instruction."
He then followed the Buddha.
Before they had entered that city, there was the Bhadrī River.
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
"I am now utterly exhausted; I shall enter the river to bathe.
At that time, the World-Honored One removed his upper robe (*uttarāsaṅga*), placed it on the riverbank, and entered the river to wash himself.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"You should with a sincere mind contemplate the thirty-two marks of the Tathāgata’s body, which thus adorns this very form; after three months, I shall enter nirvana."
Again, he addressed Ānanda:

"You should further contemplate the body of the Tathāgata: it is like the udumbara flower, which appears only after a vast interval of time; appearing but once at rare intervals, it is difficult to produce and difficult to see.
Even so, this Buddha-body surpasses that flower by hundreds of thousands of millions of times, being difficult to produce and difficult to see."
"A body such as this shall not appear again for three months.
He further addressed Ānanda:

"You should further contemplate the body of the Tathāgata: it is like a garland-maker who takes threads for stringing flowers, various colored blossoms and various fragrances, and weaves them into a flower garland; once that garland is completed, all who behold it rejoice."

The body of the Tathāgata is adorned with the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor characteristics; it possesses the golden hue of Jambūdvīpa, with radiant flames and a circular halo extending one fathom.
"Such a body as this shall enter parinirvāṇa after three months.
He further addressed Ānanda:
"You should further contemplate the body of the Tathāgata; it is like the ground where the Trāyastriṃśa gods dwell, adorned with a hundred jewels and filled with various kinds of music and joy."
Those devas cannot bear to part even for a moment from that jeweled ground and its celestial music, nor can they fully take in the colors of the jewels upon that ground;
likewise, the thirty-two marks of the Buddha’s body cannot be fully observed.
Why is this? Because as he contemplates each individual mark, his mind cannot let go.
Such a body as this shall enter parinirvāṇa after three months.
Again, he addressed Ānanda:

"You should further contemplate the body of the Tathāgata. For example, the sun and moon possess great majesty, supernatural powers, and radiance, yet when they are near the Buddha, they are completely eclipsed and do not appear. Therefore, the Buddha’s body surpasses those of the sun and moon, being most honored and most supreme."
"A body such as this shall enter parinirvāṇa three months from now.
He further addressed Ānanda:
"It is like the lion, the king among all beasts; it is like Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the great Airāvata elephant, the king among all elephants."
"The Buddha's body is likewise; endowed with great power, it walks alone without fear.
Such a body shall enter parinirvāṇa three months hence.
He further addressed Ānanda:

“You should further contemplate the body of the Tathāgata: it is composed of the four jewels like Sumeru, the king of mountains; it abides in the great ocean, remaining steadfast and unmoving, its substance solid and without flaw or fissure.”
The body of the Tathāgata surpasses the strength of Nārāyaṇa by hundreds of thousands of millions of times, beyond all comparison.
Such a body as this shall enter parinirvāṇa in three months' time.
Again, he addressed Ānanda:

“Among beings without feet, with two feet, or with many feet; among those with form and those without form; and among those with perception, without perception, or neither with nor without perception—the physical body of the Tathāgata is the most honored and the most supreme.”
"A body such as this shall enter parinirvāṇa in three months' time.
He further addressed Ānanda:

"Just as in a small chiliocosm there are a thousand suns, a thousand moons, a thousand Sumeru mountains, a thousand Pūrvavidehas, a thousand Aparagoyanīs, a thousand Uttarakurus, a thousand Jambudvīpas, a thousand Cāturmahārājakāyika heavens, a thousand Trāyastriṃśa heavens, a thousand Śakras, a thousand Yāma heavens, a thousand Yāma kings, a thousand Tuṣita heavens, a thousand Tuṣita kings, a thousand Nirmāṇarati heavens, a thousand Nirmāṇarati kings, a thousand Paranirmitavaśavartin heavens, a thousand Paranirmitavaśavartin kings, and a thousand Brahmakāyika heavens, a thousand Mahābrahmās, and a thousand Mahābrahma kings—so it is with all the devas filling such a small chiliocosm; though they wish to see the Tathāgata’s face completely and exhaustively, they are unable to see it."
Why is this? The radiance from the Tathāgata’s face is like hundreds of thousands of flashes of lightning, surpassing all the lights in the world by hundreds of thousands of millions of times.
For this reason, Śakra, the Great Brahmā, and others constantly praise the excellence of the Buddha’s radiance.
"A body such as this shall enter parinirvāṇa in three months' time.
He further addressed Ānanda:
"Do not harbor such thoughts; it is not because the Tathāgata has not exhausted greed, hatred, and delusion that he praises his own person."

The body of the Tathāgata is such that the latent tendencies of greed, hatred, and delusion, along with their residual impressions, have been forever extinguished without remainder. Thus it is, Ānanda!
The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha possesses great majestic power; you have constantly served and attended the physical body of the Tathāgata.
The merit obtained through these causes and conditions is immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, and infinitely boundless asaṃkhyeya.

“Ānanda! Do you now wish to hear the account of the causes and conditions regarding how future sentient beings will make offerings to the Tathāgata’s fragmented bodily relics after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa?
At that time, Ānanda bared his right shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Now is precisely the right time.
Great Virtuous Bhagavān!”
Now is precisely the right time.

I only pray that the Tathāgata will, for my sake, proclaim the causes and conditions regarding how all sentient beings after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa shall make offerings to the Tathāgata’s relic-sharīras.
"Having heard this Dharma, I shall receive and uphold it with a sincere heart and explain it extensively for others.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Listen well and attentively!"
I shall now speak, Ānanda!
When the Tathāgata enters nirvāṇa, he enters the Vajra-samādhi and shatters this physical body until it is like mustard seeds.
In this manner, a portion of the *śarīra* was brought to the abodes of the devas.

At that time, Śakra, King of the Devas, and the assembly of devas, seeing the Buddha’s *śarīra* and knowing that the Buddha had entered *nirvāṇa*, immediately rained down *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, *mañjūṣaka* flowers, and *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers as an offering to the *śarīra*. As if they were beholding the Buddha’s own body, they prostrated and circumambulated it to the right; some planted the roots of goodness for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, some planted the roots of goodness of the *śrāvaka*, and some planted the roots of goodness of the *pratyekabuddha*.

"One portion of the *śarīra* was directed toward the world of the nāgas. At that time, the Nāga King Sāgara and immeasurable other nāgas, seeing the Buddha’s *śarīra*, made extensive offerings. Using *indranīla* jewels, *mahendranīla* jewels, fire-jewels, water-purifying jewels, and such immeasurable varieties of precious gems, they used them to make offerings to the fragmented *śarīra*.

Having performed prostrations, circumambulations, and offerings, the nāgas each made their own vows: some vowed for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, some vowed for the enlightenment of a *śrāvaka*, and some vowed for the enlightenment of a *pratyekabuddha*."

"One portion of the śarīra was directed toward the world of the yakṣas. At that time, King Vaiśravaṇa and other immeasurable great yakṣa generals, seeing the fragmented śarīra, made offerings to it with various kinds of flowers, powdered incense, burning incense, lamps, and music. Thus they made immeasurable offerings to the śarīra, prostrating, joining their palms, circumambulating it to the right, and paying homage with reverence;
some conceived the vow for unexcelled great bodhi, some conceived the vow of a śrāvaka, and some conceived the vow of a pratyekabuddha."
"The remaining relics of his shall remain in Jambudvīpa; in the future, there will be a king named Aśoka who will unify Jambudvīpa.
For the sake of making offerings to these relics, this king shall construct eighty-four thousand stūpas and enshrine these relics therein for worship."

In this Jambudvīpa, there will likewise be sixty thousand kings who shall also make offerings to the *śarīra* relics of the pulverized body. With various flower garlands, diverse incenses, lamps, and music, they shall offer worship, prostrate, circumambulate to the right, and pay homage.

Some shall plant the roots of goodness for unsurpassed great bodhi; some shall plant the roots of goodness of the śrāvakas; and some shall plant the roots of goodness of the pratyekabuddhas. Some shall immediately renounce their homes to go forth into homelessness, possessing pure faith within the Buddha-dharma, shaving off their hair and beards and donning the dharma robes, diligently practicing the path until all outflows are exhausted and they enter parinirvāṇa.
"In this way, Ānanda!

The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha possesses great majestic power. Because that Dharma-body relies upon the birth-body, the merit obtained through the causes and conditions of making offerings to the relics of the birth-body is immeasurable, boundless, incalculable, and inexpressible."
At that time, the Tathāgata had this thought:

"In order that this Buddha-dharma, which I have accomplished through diligent toil over three asaṃkhyeya kalpas, may long abide in the world, I shall go to the abodes of the devas, asuras, nāgas, garuḍas, mahoragas, and others, and entrust the Buddha-dharma to them."
At that time, the Tathāgata vanished from Jambudvīpa and appeared in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
When Śakra, King of the Devas, saw the World-Honored One, he immediately prepared a high throne to welcome the Tathāgata and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"I pray that you will accept this seat.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One sat upon the seat.
Śakra, King of Devas, together with hundreds of thousands of millions of beings, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and stood to one side.
The Buddha addressed Śakra, saying:
"You should now know that I, too, shall soon enter parinirvāṇa; I entrust this Buddha-dharma to you, and you must protect and uphold it."
Thus he spoke up to three times.
Śakra Devānām Indra, weeping until his face was drenched with tears, wiped away his tears and said:
"How swift is the Parinirvāṇa of the World-Honored One!"
"How exceedingly swift is the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa!

The Dharma-eye of the world is forever extinguished herein. As for that which the Buddha has taught as being within our capacity, we shall immediately protect, uphold, revere, and make offerings to it."
In the past, when the Tathāgata descended from the Tuṣita Heaven into his mother’s womb, I, together with the hosts of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, constantly provided protection;
likewise, at the time of the Buddha’s birth, I also came with the various devas to provide protection;

and when the Tathāgata sat beneath the Bodhi tree and destroyed the armies of eight hundred million *koṭis* of Māras, attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I and the various devas also constantly provided protection.
"When the Buddha turned the Wheel of Dharma with its three revolutions and twelve aspects in the Deer Park at Vārāṇasī, I and the hosts of devas also constantly provided protection.
Yet, even now, I lack the power to prevent the Tathāgata from entering nirvāṇa, nor do I have the power to protect him."

At that time, the World-Honored One preached various teachings, exhorting, comforting, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening Śakra and the devas, causing them to protect the Buddha-dharma. He then vanished from the heavens and immediately appeared in the palace of the Naga King Sāgara.
At that time, when the Dragon King saw the Tathāgata arrive, he immediately prepared a seat.
The Buddha sat upon the seat and addressed the Dragon King, saying:
"You should know now that the Tathāgata will soon enter parinirvāṇa."
I entrust the Buddha-dharma to you; you should protect it and ensure that it is not severed.

Nāga King, you should know that in this world of nāgas there are many evil nāgas who frequently give rise to anger and do not understand the distinction between sin and merit. They act with sudden violence to destroy my Dharma; for this reason, I now entrust this Buddha-dharma to you.
At that time, the Dragon King wept, his tears falling like rain upon his face; he wiped away his tears and said, “World-Honored One!
We dragons are blind, lacking the eye of wisdom; for this reason, we have now been born among the animals.”
If, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, the world of the dragons becomes empty and we give up our lives, we shall not know where we will be reborn in the future.
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are the jewels of sentient beings; why now do you wish to enter parinirvāṇa, causing the Eye of the World to perish?

At that time, the World-Honored One instructed, exhorted, benefited, and gladdened King Sāgara, causing him to protect the Buddha-dharma; he then vanished from the dragon palace and appeared in the palace of the Dragon King Takṣaka.
At that time, the Dragon King prepared a seat for the Buddha, and the Buddha sat upon it.
The Dragon King, together with a hundred trillion dragons, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to stand to one side. The Buddha addressed the Dragon King:
“You should know that before long the Tathāgata will enter the realm of outflows and pass into parinirvāṇa. I now entrust the Buddha-dharma to you; protect it with a sincere heart.”
At that time, the Dragon King wept so bitterly that his tears fell like rain; wiping away his tears with his hand, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"When the Tathāgata enters parinirvāṇa, the eye of the world will perish. The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are the jewels of sentient beings."
"If the Buddha passes into parinirvāṇa, I do not know where I shall be reborn.
The Buddha preached various teachings for the dragon king, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening him; he then vanished from that place and reappeared within the palace of the Black Dragon King.

At that time, the Dragon King prepared a seat for the Buddha; the Buddha sat upon it, and the Black Dragon King, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of dragons, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to stand to one side.
The Buddha told the Dragon King:
"You should know that the Tathāgata will soon enter parinirvāṇa. I entrust the Buddha-dharma to you; you must protect it with a sincere heart."
At that time, the Dragon King wept, wiping his tears with his face and speaking thus:

"With the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, the eye of the world is extinguished. The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are the jewels of sentient beings; if the Buddha passes into extinction, I do not know where I shall be born hereafter."
The Buddha taught the Dharma to them, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening them; he then vanished from that place and appeared in the world of the yakṣas.
At that time, King Vaiśravaṇa prepared a seat for the Buddha, and the Buddha sat upon it.
King Vaiśravaṇa, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, King Virūḍhaka, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of kumbhāṇḍas, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the Celestial King Virūpākṣa, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of nāgas, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the Celestial King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of gandharvas, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit to one side.

At that time, the great yakṣa generals—Pañcika, Cārūṇḍa, Satagiri, Haimavata, Maṇibhadra, and Pūrṇabhadra—as well as all such yakṣa generals, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Four Great Kings, as well as the generals of the yakṣas, the generals of the gandharvas, the generals of the kumbhāṇḍas, and the generals of the nāgas, saying:
"You should know that the Tathāgata will soon enter parinirvāṇa."
"I entrust the Buddha-dharma to you; you must guard it well.
He said this a second and a third time.

"You should know that within the realm of yakṣas there are evil yakṣas, in the realm of kumbhāṇḍas there are evil kumbhāṇḍas, in the realm of gandharvas there are evil gandharvas, and in the lands of the nāgas there are evil nāgas. Such beings frequently give rise to anger, do not understand the distinction between sin and merit, and act with wicked violence, thereby destroying the unsurpassed Buddha-dharma that I have cultivated through diligent suffering for three asaṃkhyeya kalpas. For this reason, I now entrust it to you."
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings, the yakṣa generals, and even the nāga generals wept until their faces were drenched; wiping away their tears, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, why is your parinirvāṇa so exceedingly swift?"
"How swift is the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa!
He has been swallowed by the makara of death.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having taught, instructed, benefited, and gladdened them with various discourses on the Dharma, immediately vanished from there and emerged in Jambudvīpa.
At that time, the World-Honored One had this thought:
"The task I set for myself is now completed; all wicked sentient beings have now been subdued. I may now enter the peaceful, quiescent nirvana."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Saṃsāra is to be loathed; I shall soon enter parinirvāṇa.

At that time, Ānanda was overcome with great anguish; his face was drenched with tears of grief as if arrows were piercing his heart. He fainted and fell prostrate, rolling upon the ground, and spoke these words:
"How exceedingly swift is the Parinirvāṇa of the World-Honored One?
How rapid is the extinction of the Tathāgata!
The Eye of the World has been extinguished; with whom shall I now go to receive my almsbowl?"
Furthermore, with whom shall I stand holding this fan?
From whom shall I no longer hear the Dharma of the Deathless (amṛta)? Who will again speak to me of the flavor of the Deathless?
Whose footsteps shall I follow from now on?

We shall no longer behold that most excellent, full moon-like face. The Venerable Śāriputra and other great beings of vast wisdom have already entered *nirvāṇa*, and now the Buddha-Tathāgata is likewise passing into extinction.

The world has become shrouded in darkness, losing the eye of wisdom; the Wisdom-Sumeru King is now about to crumble, the Buddha-tree is about to fall, the bridge of Dharma is about to snap, the ship of Dharma is about to sink, and the torch of Dharma is about to be extinguished. The sun and moon of the True Dharma are about to fall to the earth; the gate of liberation is now about to be closed, while the gates of the three evil realms are about to open. The accumulation of the Dharma gathered over three *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas will soon perish.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Elder Ānanda:
"Do not grieve; do not weep further; do not cry out loudly, beat your breast, choke with sobs, faint, or fall to the ground."

Why is this? That which is born in the world is a conditioned phenomenon (*saṃskṛta-dharma*) that inevitably returns to impermanence; to wish for such a phenomenon not to be lost or destroyed, but to remain eternally constant, is impossible.

At that time, the World-Honored One preached the Dharma in various ways, comforting, exhorting, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening them; having entrusted the treasury of the Dharma, he remained silent.
Then the World-Honored One thought again:
"The bhikṣu Ānanda has been pierced by the thorn of sorrow deep within his heart; I shall now extract that thorn of sorrow for him."
He addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Do you wish now to see the events of the future?
I perceive the coming age as clearly as I behold the present; I shall explain it for you."
At that time, Ānanda bared his right shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Virtuous World-Honored One!
"Please speak for my sake; now is the very time.
Having heard the Dharma, I shall receive, uphold, and widely propagate it.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Listen attentively and with a sincere mind; I shall now speak. Ānanda!

In the future, there will be monks who violate the precepts, wearing the *kāṣāya* robe as they wander through cities and towns, coming and going among villages and staying in the homes of their relatives. They are neither true monks nor laypeople, yet they keep wives and concubines and procreate sons and daughters.”
Furthermore, there were bhikṣus who lived in the houses of courtesans;
there were bhikṣus who committed sexual misconduct with bhikṣuṇīs;
and there were bhikṣus who stored gold and silver and engaged in worldly occupations to sustain their lives.
Furthermore, there were bhikṣus who sustained their livelihood by serving as couriers and messengers;
others who sustained their livelihood by specializing in medical practice;
and still others who sustained their livelihood by playing go and six-man chess.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who sustain their lives by practicing divination and fortune-telling for others;
furthermore, there are bhikṣus who sustain their lives by casting spells over corpses to raise them up and dispatching them to kill enemies on behalf of others;
furthermore, there are bhikṣus who sustain their lives by reciting incantations to exorcise spirits and ghosts for others while taking a great deal of wealth.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who sustain their lives by specializing in taking life;
there are bhikṣus who reside in monasteries and privately expend the property of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha to sustain their own lives;
and there are bhikṣus who, while inwardly actually violating the precepts, outwardly pretend to uphold them while receiving the faithful offerings of others.

Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who, though they do not break the precepts, harbor stinginess and parsimony; regarding clothing, food, drink, and even the property of the Saṃgha, they begrudge it and do not give it to visiting monks.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who, though they do not break the precepts, are miserly regarding the dwellings and bedding of the Saṃgha and do not give them to visiting monks.

Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who, though they do not break the precepts, receive great wealth and profit through the offerings and prostrations of various donors; their hearts do not wish for other bhikṣus to receive the faithful offerings of others, desiring only to receive them themselves.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who, though not actually arhats, constantly falsely claim to have attained the fruit of arhatship, desiring that others know them to be arhats;

furthermore, there are bhikṣus who receive abundant offerings of the four requisites from donors, yet possess no genuine virtue within while only increasing their greed, seeking merely to sustain their lives rather than to cultivate the Path;
furthermore, there are bhikṣus who engage in trade and commerce for profit in order to support themselves.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who sustain themselves exclusively by practicing theft;
there are bhikṣus who raise elephants, horses, camels, donkeys, oxen, and sheep, even engaging in buying and selling to sustain themselves;
and there are bhikṣus who sustain themselves by trafficking in male and female slaves.
Furthermore, there were bhikṣus who sustained themselves by slaughtering oxen and sheep;
others who accepted recruitment to enter battle, waging war and conducting expeditions to kill many people in pursuit of merit and rewards;
and yet others who breached walls and overcame fortifications to steal the property of others for their own livelihood.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who devote themselves exclusively to robbery, plundering cities and villages to sustain their lives;
and there are bhikṣus who destroy Buddhist stūpas, taking their precious contents to sustain their lives.
Through such immeasurable causes and conditions for rebirth in hell, after they relinquish their lives, they all fall into hell. "Ānanda!

For example, when a lion’s life has ended and its body is dead—whether in the air, on the ground, in the water, or on land—no sentient beings dare to eat the flesh of that lion's body; only various worms born from the lion's own body will devour the lion's flesh."

Ānanda! My Buddha-dharma cannot be destroyed by others; rather, it is the evil bhikṣus within my own teaching who are like poisonous thorns, destroying the Buddha-dharma accumulated through the diligent practice of three asaṃkhyeya kalpas.

Ānanda! It is like a person who enters the great ocean, reaches an island of jewels, gathers many precious objects, and places them upon a ship; yet while wishing to cross the great ocean, he sinks therein.

The True Dharma of the Buddha is like that precious ship; in the future, many evil bhikṣus who break the precepts will take great pleasure in committing various kinds of evil deeds, causing my Buddha-dharma to perish and sink out of sight.

“Ānanda! Not long after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall fall into disorder. Once the True Dharma has fallen into disorder, various kinds of wicked bhikṣus will appear in the world who do not believe that the Tathāgata has realized the untainted, quiescent nirvāṇa, let alone believing that other people in the world have attained arhatship and entered nirvāṇa.”

Ānanda! All the True Dharma of the Tathāgata—consisting of the names, phrases, and meanings of the twelve divisions of scripture, namely: Sūtra, Geya, Vyākaraṇa, Gāthā, Udāna, Nidāna, Avadāna, Itivṛttaka, Jātaka, Vaipulya, Adbhutadharma, and Upadeśa—will be destroyed by wicked bhikṣus; for those people delight in composing literary works and adorning their speech with flowery rhetoric.
"There are many such evil bhikṣus who will destroy my Buddha-dharma.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
"In future ages, will such evil bhikṣus who break the precepts be born?
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is!"
Ānanda! In future ages, there will appear in the world such evil bhikṣus who, though they don the dharma robes and shave their hair and beards, will destroy my Buddha-dharma.
At that time, Ānanda had this thought:
"By the power of the Buddha, might I be able to see such events in future ages?
Then, through his supernormal powers, the Tathāgata caused Ānanda to see all those evil bhikṣus of the future, with their sons sitting on their laps and their wives placed by their sides.
Furthermore, he saw various kinds of unlawful matters.
At that time, having seen these things, Ānanda was struck with great fear and his hair stood on end; he immediately addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“The Tathāgata shall swiftly enter parinirvāṇa; now is precisely the right time. What is the use of seeing such evil events of this future world?
The Buddha said to Ānanda: “What do you think?”
“Regarding what the Tathāgata has just said concerning the retribution for the evil karma of wicked bhikṣus— could this possibly be known by anyone else?
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying,
“World-Honored One!”
"Only the Tathāgata is able to know the retributions for these various evil karmas in future ages.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!"
Ānanda! It is exactly as you have said; only a Tathāgata can truly know this. Ānanda!
"Do you now see any instance where the Tathāgata, while not yet having entered parinirvāṇa, was surrounded by wicked bhikṣus as he preached the Dharma to them?
Ānanda replied, "There has never been such a thing."
The Buddha said, “Ānanda, excellent, excellent!”
"It is as you have said.
In the present, there are truly no such evil bhikṣus surrounding the Tathāgata while the Buddha preaches the Dharma for them.
The Buddha said:
“Ānanda! In future ages, many laypeople in white robes will attain rebirth in the heavens, while many who have gone forth as monastics will fall into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals.”
He further addressed Ānanda:
"The karma of good and evil never perishes.

In the past, when I was a merchant leader, I entered the great ocean and killed one person with my own hands for the sake of saving many others. Due to the causal conditions of this karma, even until my attainment of Buddhahood, I still experienced the retribution of being struck by a golden spear."

At that time, Śakra, King of the Devas, together with the assembly of the Thirty-three Heavens, quickly went to where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to stand to one side.
Yama, King of the Devas, together with an assembly of a hundred trillion Yāma devas, quickly went to where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.

The Deva King of Tuṣita, together with a multitude of a hundred trillion Tuṣita devas, quickly went to the place where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.

The King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, together with a multitude of one hundred trillion Nirmāṇarati devas, quickly went to the place where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.

The King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, together with a multitude of one hundred trillion Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, quickly went to the place where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.

At that time, the asura king Vemacitra, together with a multitude of one hundred trillion asuras, quickly went to where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the Naga King Sagara, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of nāgas, quickly went to where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.

All of them, in a single thought-moment, a single kṣaṇa, and a single muhūrta, filled the sky for twelve yojanas—devas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others—all because they wished to see the Tathāgata for the last time.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda:
“This site of enlightenment, the Bodhi tree, is most supreme and exquisite; all Buddhas of the past have realized anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi at this very place.”
Future Buddhas will also attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* at this very place.
Now, in my own person, I have likewise attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* at this place, having defeated eighteen billion demonic armies.
Thus it is, Ānanda!
I shall now soon enter parinirvāṇa.
Furthermore, Ānanda!
The Lumbinī Garden is most excellent and most wondrous; it is the place where the Buddha, the Tathāgata, took his final birth.
Furthermore, Ānanda, Lady Māyā possessed great merit and virtue, such that she was able to give birth to a treasure among men.
Furthermore, Ānanda!
King Śuddhodana possesses great merit and virtue; he is the most excellent jewel among all sentient beings, acting as their father.
Furthermore, Ānanda!

The city of Vaiśālī is the most excellent and wondrous among the countries of Videha; the great city of Rājagṛha is the most excellent and wondrous among the country of Magadha; the site of the seven *āmra* trees is likewise wondrous; the site of the *goḍama-nyagrodha* tree is likewise excellent and wondrous; the resting place of Pailā, Drāḍa, and Drauṇi is likewise excellent and wondrous;

and the birthplace of the Mallas is where the past Wheel-Turning Sage Kings removed their jeweled celestial crowns to enshrine them here as stūpas for the *pratyekabuddhas*. This is the most excellent and wondrous ground for me to cremate my body.
Furthermore, Ānanda!
This Jambudvīpa is the most excellent and superior place; therein sentient beings delight in and crave long life. For this reason, I shall now enter parinirvāṇa here.
"The Dharma I have accumulated over three *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas shall soon perish.
At that time, the World-Honored One comforted Ānanda, causing his heart to rejoice and removing the thorn of his grief.
Having completed the entrustment of the Dharma, he addressed Ānanda, saying:
"I shall now go with you to various kingdoms.
Ānanda replied, "So be it," and accepted the Tathāgata’s instruction.
At that time, the World-Honored One arrived at the city of Pāpā and completed the deliverance of all those who were to be saved there.
He then traveled to various other kingdoms, where he taught and transformed immeasurable hundreds of billions of nayutas of sentient beings, bringing them all to full accomplishment.

At that time, Ānanda followed behind the Buddha as they proceeded in this manner until they reached the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment in the kingdom of Magadha. Having circumambulated the tree six times, the World-Honored One sat down beneath it in the full lotus posture.
The Buddha told Ānanda, “In no long time, on the fifteenth day of the month, the Tathāgata shall enter parinirvāṇa.
At that time, the devas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others had this thought:
"The Tathāgata will enter parinirvāṇa before long on the fifteenth day; we shall all perform our final prostrations.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Do not harbor such a thought."
"It is said that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, while possessing greed, hatred, and delusion, praised this region of Jambudvīpa;
yet the Tathāgata is actually free from greed, hatred, and delusion."

These three realms are the places where sentient beings are born. Within these three realms, this desire realm is where sentient beings practice the three types of evil karma, as well as create the karma for human and celestial rebirths, the karma of the form realm and the formless realm, and even the karma of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
Having spoken these words, the Buddha rose from his seat.
At that very moment, this earth shook in six ways, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of devas, weeping with sorrow in the midst of the sky, spoke thus:
"Such a jewel among sentient beings shall soon pass away."
The Lotus-Face Sūtra, Scroll Upper;
The Lotus-Face Sūtra, Scroll Lower.
Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas.
At that time, the World-Honored One departed from the Bodhi tree.

King Vaiśravaṇa, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful wailing and shed tears like rain; wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke these verses:
“The Tathāgata’s countenance is most subtle and wondrous, Surpassing all beings, peerless and incomparable.”
"With a body thus adorned and so extraordinary, you shall enter parinirvāṇa before long.

At that time, Śakra, King of the Devas, together with hundreds of thousands of billions of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, simultaneously raised their voices in sorrowful weeping, shedding tears like rain; wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke in verse:
"The Tathāgata’s face is perfectly full and round, His form and color surpassing the sun and moon;"
"The one worthy of offerings by all gods and men— We shall no longer be able to behold him.

At that time, the Heavenly King Suyāma, together with a multitude of a hundred trillion Suyāma devas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, raining down tears; wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke these verses:
"In human form, most heroic and fierce in diligence, His majestic power can shatter all demonic armies;
“The Lion of the Śākyas, born from the lineage of sugarcane, is now being devoured by impermanence.

At that time, the Tuṣita Heaven was joined by a multitude of a hundred trillion Tuṣita devas, who simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, raining down tears as they wiped them away with their hands, and spoke these verses:
“He whom those who behold him never tire of seeing is like a King of Medicine; his appearance in the world is like a great, brilliant lamp.”
"Now that the Eye of Wisdom has entered parinirvāṇa, the world shall once again be shrouded in total darkness.

At that time, the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, together with a multitude of one hundred trillion Nirmāṇarati devas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping; shedding tears like rain, they wiped away their tears with their hands and spoke these verses:
"With steady gait, unmoving, more majestic than a lion; His countenance perfect and full, surpassing the form of the moon."
"Once again he shall not tread upon this ground; the footprints marked with the thousand-spoked wheels shall never be seen again.

At that time, Māra, the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, was filled with great joy and felt profound peace and happiness. Together with a multitude of one hundred trillion Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, he quickly went to where the Buddha was and joined his palms toward the Buddha.
And he spoke in verse:
"All evil beings have already been subdued; all great coarseness and ferocity are forever gone without remainder.
For what reason do you still remain in this world? We only pray that the Tathāgata will quickly enter parinirvāṇa."
At that time, the Great Brahmā King became incensed with the Māra King and spoke these words: "Alas!
O Māra King, you most wicked of beings!"
"The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are the most supreme jewels; why do you now wish for the World-Honored One to enter parinirvāṇa so quickly?

At that time, the Great Brahmā King, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of Brahmā devas, simultaneously raised their voices in piteous weeping, shedding tears like rain, and wiping away their tears with their hands, spoke these verses:
"In this present world and in the future, In the Brahmā worlds and other celestial realms;..."
"Never before have we seen such a body as the Buddha’s—so pure, complete, and with a face so dignified and majestic.

At that time, Vemacitra, the Asura King, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of Asuras, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, raining down tears as they wiped them away with their hands, and spoke these verses:
"The merit of the Buddha’s form is immeasurable; No one can reach its ultimate limit."
"You will benefit the asuras and other realms; if you were to enter parinirvāṇa now, the world would become empty.

At that time, the Dragon King Sāgara, together with hundreds of billions of dragon hosts, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, raining down tears and wiping them away with their hands, as they spoke this verse:
"Even a thousand elephants like Airāvata Are not equal to the strength of a single joint of the Tathāgata."
"One so powerful, heroic, and fierce, is now destroyed by impermanence.

At that time, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of kumbhāṇḍas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping; shedding tears like rain, they wiped away their tears with their hands and spoke this verse:
"Homage to the Great Awakened One, the Wondrous Lotus, Born from that pool of pure precepts!"
"Manifesting the sign of impermanence, he shall soon fall into eternal extinction.

At that time, the Deva King Virūpākṣa, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of nāgas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping; raining down tears, they wiped them away with their hands and spoke these verses:
"The Tathāgata’s countenance is like the full moon, His radiant light shines like the orb of the sun."
"Thus he will not remain long in this world, showing himself as devoured by impermanence.

At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping; shedding tears like rain, they wiped away their tears with their hands and spoke these verses:
"The Buddha’s body is golden and most sublime, Adorned naturally with the thirty-two marks; The Buddha’s body is golden and most sublime, Adorned naturally with the thirty-two marks;"
"Before long, he shall fall under the power of impermanence, Destroying the pure Great Muni.

At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of nāgas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, shedding tears like rain; wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke these verses:
"The physical form and color of the Tathāgata are most rare, Without peer within the three realms."
"In this way, before long you shall enter parinirvāṇa, caught in the snare of impermanence.

At that time, the great yakṣa general named Pañcika, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, shedding tears like rain. Wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke these verses:
"The Buddha’s voice is supreme, surpassing that of Brahmā; It exceeds even the song of the kalaviṅka bird."
"The Tathāgata will soon enter parinirvāṇa; we shall no longer hear the Dharma of the Deathless.

At that time, the yakṣa general named Pañcāla, together with a multitude of a hundred trillion yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, shedding tears like rain. Wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke these verses:
"The World-Honored One possesses a body of golden radiance, And a face like the full moon, adorned with merit."
"The mark of the white tuft between the eyebrows is most extraordinary; I now pay homage to you for the last time.

At that moment, the great yakṣa general Maṇibhadra, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, shedding tears like rain. Wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke these verses:
"Thirty-two supreme and wondrous marks, And eighty minor characteristics adorn you naturally;
"You shall become the Vajra Lord of Impermanence, Shattering the Great Sage, the Honored Muni.

At that time, the great yakṣa general Pūrṇabhadra, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, shedding tears like rain. Wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke in verse:
"All Buddhas of the past, And all World-Honored Ones of the future;
"The Lion-King of the Śākyas of great power has been harmed by the lion of impermanence.

At that time, the great yakṣa general Maśīlidika, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, raining down tears as they wiped them away with their hands, and spoke these verses:
"I now see the Muni for the last time; From this moment on, I shall never behold him again."
"Finally, he prostrates at the Buddha’s thousand-spoked wheel, making all the mounds and hollows level with his feet.

At that time, the great yakṣa general Khaṭāraṅga, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, shedding tears like rain; wiping away their tears with their hands, they spoke this verse:
"Alas! How great is the evil mark of impermanence, Which destroys all sentient beings!"
“Such a supreme jewel among sentient beings, Will likewise enter nirvana and not remain long.

At that time, the great yakṣa general named Kumbhīra, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, simultaneously raised their voices in mournful weeping, raining down tears as they wiped them away with their hands, and spoke these verses:
“I now take refuge and pay homage to the Buddha-tree, Born from the great earth of moral discipline;”
"It shall become the axe and halberd of impermanence, Before long felling the Great Muni.
At that time, the great yakṣa general Satakiṛi, together with a host of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, wept bitterly, raining down tears; wiping away his tears with his hands, he spoke in verse:
"The mark of the white tuft between the brows Shines resplendently like the orb of the moon;"
"His eyes are as pure as blue lotuses; rare indeed, we shall not see him again.
At that time, the Earth Deity, together with a multitude of a hundred trillion yakṣas, wept with sorrow, raining down tears, and wiping them away with their hands, spoke these verses:
"I now pay homage to the heroic and fierce one, the most excellent among men;"
"Supreme among those with two feet, I pay homage to the Great Muni.
At that time, the deity of the Bodhi tree wept with tears falling like rain; wiping away her tears with her hand, she spoke this verse:
"In this place, the King of Māra was defeated, along with his demonic retinue."
"Before long, the Great Muni will be extinguished by the demon of impermanence.
At that time, the deity of the Jeta Grove wept with tears falling like rain; wiping away his tears with his hand, he spoke this verse:
"The Jeta Grove shall be empty, and the Bamboo Grove shall be likewise."
"The pit of impermanence is exceedingly deep; the Tathāgata has entered it and is no longer seen.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, together with a multitude of hundreds of billions of yakṣas, wept with tears falling like rain, wiped away their tears with their hands, and spoke these verses:
"Such is this most excellent city, and it is also a land of great abundance;"
"Having abandoned the Śākya clan, toward what destination shall you go?
At that time, the goddess of the Lumbinī grove wept with tears falling like rain; wiping away her tears with her hand, she spoke this verse:
"The King Śuddhodana has already passed away, And Queen Māyā has likewise entered parinirvāṇa."
"The Tathāgata now desires to enter nirvāṇa; such quiescence is invisible.
At that time, the deity of Kapilavastu hastened to the Buddha's presence, weeping with tears falling like rain and rolling upon the ground, speaking these words:
"How exceedingly swift is the Tathāgata’s nirvāṇa! How rapid is the World-Honored One’s entry into nirvāṇa!"
"The Eye of the World has perished," he said, and spoke this verse:
"In the Lumbinī Grove was the Buddha’s birthplace; He grew to maturity in the city of Kapilavastu."
"His radiance surpasses that of a thousand suns; now we see him for the last time, and shall not see him again.
At that moment, the Bodhi-tree deity, together with the devas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, raised a great cry from the midst of the sky, wailing and lamenting, saying:
"The Buddha is the most supreme treasure among sentient beings; he shall soon pass away."
At that time, the World-Honored One uttered a Brahma-voice and addressed the assembly of devas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, and mahoragas, saying:
"Do not weep; do not utter such strange words; do not give rise to grief and affliction by beating your breasts with your hands until your hearts become bewildered and distressed."
How could there be any being in the world who, having taken birth, could cause conditioned phenomena produced by the harmony of causes and conditions to endure for long?
If one wishes to forcibly prevent these impermanent phenomena from disintegrating, such a thing is impossible.

At that time, having instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened the devas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, mahoragas, and others, the World-Honored One caused them to rejoice; thereupon, the devas down to the mahoragas circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right and returned to their respective abodes.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"In the past, at the abode of the Naga King Apalāla, I prophesied regarding the kingdom of Kaśmīra: 'After my parinirvāṇa, that kingdom shall flourish, be peaceful and secure, and enjoy abundance and joy like Uttarakuru. The Buddha-dharma shall flourish there, with many arhats dwelling in that land, as well as immeasurable disciples of the Tathāgata.'"
All the arhats residing in this Jambudvīpa went to that land, which was like the Tuṣita heaven.
There, they compiled the twelve divisions of the Tathāgata’s teachings—namely:
sūtra, geya, vyākaraṇa, gāthā, udāna, nidāna, avadāna, itivṛttaka, jātaka, vaipulya, adbhutadharma, and upadeśa—and extensively composed various treatises.
That kingdom of Kaśmīra is like the Nandana Grove of Śakra, and also like the Anavatapta Lake of Cool Purity.
Furthermore, there are those such as Phalguna and Piṇḍola who all delight in dwelling in that land of Kaśmīra.
Arhats who have not regressed from the Buddha-vehicle also dwell in that land.

Furthermore, there are Arhats such as Indramāṇava and Śvetagrīva, who, regarding the Dharma-treasury taught by the Tathāgata—both the out-flowing (sāsrava) and the non-out-flowing (anāsrava) dharmas—have compiled them all and widely disseminated them.
"Ānanda! After my parinirvāṇa, these final dharmakāyas shall establish themselves for the sake of the future.

Furthermore, there are five devaputras, including Kumbhīra and others, who will be born in the land of Kaśmīra and cause my Dharma to spread widely throughout the world, making great offerings such as have never before been made by my disciples in Jambudvīpa during this great assembly."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"In a future age, in the land of Kaśmīra, such a great Dharma assembly shall be held. Ānanda!"

After those five celestial sons had passed into parinirvāṇa, there was a disciple of the heretic Pūraṇa named Padmavaktra (Lotus Face). He was intelligent and wise, well-versed in the astronomy of the twenty-eight lunar mansions, the five planets, and their various degrees. His body was like the color of gold. This great fool had previously made offerings to four arhats;

at the time of making those offerings, he made this vow: "May I, in the future, destroy the Buddha-dharma; and because I have made offerings to the arhats, may I receive a handsome body in every successive lifetime."
"In his final birth, he will be born into a royal family and become a king named Maitrakanyaka, who shall destroy my Dharma.
This great fool shall shatter my bowl, and having shattered the bowl, he will be reborn in the Avīci Great Hell."

After this great fool passed away, seven devaputras successively cast off their bodies and were reborn in the kingdom of Kaśmīra; they further established the True Dharma of the Tathāgata and made grand offerings.
Ānanda! Because of the broken bowl, my disciples will gradually defile their pure precepts.
When the bowl first breaks, although the bhikṣus may defile their pure precepts, they will possess wisdom like that of a bull-king and be able to defeat the followers of external paths.

During the second period, the bhikṣus of this Jambudvīpa will violate the pure precepts and delight in performing unwholesome deeds; they will engage in bodily acts such as theft, plowing fields, and cultivation; they will be excessively greedy for accumulating fine robes and fine alms bowls; and they will take no pleasure in reading or reciting the Sūtras, the Vinaya, or the Abhidharma.
Thus it is, Ānanda!
Those wise people who delight in reading and reciting shall all attain parinirvāṇa.
At that time, there will be many bhikṣus who are deceitful, crooked, and envious, giving rise to much that is contrary to the Dharma.
Because the bhikṣus do not act in accordance with the Dharma, the kings and others do not rely upon the royal law.
Because the kings do not govern according to the royal law, the people of that country frequently practice the ten unwholesome courses of action to an excessive degree.
Due to their evil karma, this land will abound with thorns, poisonous weeds, soil, sand, and gravel. Ānanda!
At that time, the five kinds of refined flavors in this Jambudvīpa will lose their potency and their taste—namely, clarified butter, oil, salt, rock honey, and honey.

Because these five kinds of power and flavor have thus been lost, at that time sentient beings will once again engage even more extensively in superior evil karma. Due to their extensive practice of such evil and unwholesome deeds, the Buddha’s broken bowl shall proceed to the northern region.

At that time, the sentient beings of the northern regions, seeing the Buddha break his bowl and perform a grand offering, made offerings to this bowl with various flowers, incense, ointments, lamps, garlands, and various kinds of music. Among them, some conceived the aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, some conceived the aspiration for the vehicle of the *śrāvaka*, and some conceived the aspiration for the vehicle of the *pratyekabuddha*.

That broken bowl shall go toward the country of Pāṭaliputra. When the people of that country see the Buddha’s broken bowl, they will make offerings to it with various flowers, burning incense, powdered incense, unguents, lamps, garlands, and various kinds of music. Among them, some will resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, some will resolve to become *śrāvakas*, and some will resolve to become *pratyekabuddhas*.

“Ānanda! Because of the Buddha’s power and also due to the karmic resonance of the roots of goodness of sentient beings, this broken bowl of mine has naturally returned to its original state without change. Not long thereafter, my bowl will vanish from Jambudvīpa and appear within the palace of the Nāga King Sāgara.”

At the time of his passing, this Jambudvīpa will be shrouded in great darkness for seven days and seven nights; the majestic light of the sun and moon will no longer appear, the earth will shake violently, and amidst the empty sky, evil thunder and lightning will flash while malevolent sounds resound, as a black wind suddenly arises in extreme terror.
The devas, humans, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, mahoragas, and others all wailed loudly, their tears falling like rain.
Thus it is, Ānanda!
When this bowl first sinks, the Tathāgata’s Dharma and Vinaya shall likewise sink and disappear.
At that time, seeing the extinction of the Dharma and Vinaya, the Māra King will be greatly delighted and feel profound peace in his heart, and he will speak these words from mid-air:
"Once the Dharma of Gautama has perished, I shall teach and transform all sentient beings who commit various evils themselves and also incite others to do so.
Following these teachings of Māra, cities, towns, and villages began to slaughter one another.
At that time, because Māra had extensively incited sentient beings to commit evil, his physical body fell directly into the Avīci Hell.

At that time, the Dragon King Sāgara, having seen the Buddha’s bowl, made a grand offering with various precious jewels—Indranīla gems, Mahānīla gems, fire-jewels, and water-purifying gems—and for seven days he prostrated and circumambulated it to the right.

Among these nāgas, some gave rise to the aspiration for unexcelled bodhicitta, some gave rise to the aspiration for the state of a śrāvaka, and some gave rise to the aspiration for the state of a pratyekabuddha.
At that time, the Nāga King Sāgara cupped his hands to receive the bowl and spoke this verse:
"With hands adorned by all the marks, You receive various flavors of food;..."
"Place it in this bowl and eat from it in this manner.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"In this way, my bowl vanished from the palace of the Nāga King Sāgara and appeared in the palaces of the Four Heavenly Kings."

At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings—Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Vaiśravaṇa, and Dhṛtarāṣṭra—made grand offerings for seven days and seven nights. Having offered various flowers, various garlands, various ointments, various incenses, various lamps, and various musical performances, they paid homage.
At that time, among the assembly of devas, some gave rise to the mind of unsurpassed bodhi, some gave rise to the mind of a śrāvaka, and some gave rise to the mind of a pratyekabuddha.
Then, the kumbhāṇḍa king Virūḍhaka cupped his hands to support the bowl and spoke these verses:
"The Tathāgata’s final meal Was taken at the house of the blacksmith; ... [rest of verse]"
"The bowl has come to this place in order to transform sentient beings.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"After seven days have passed, my bowl will vanish from the palaces of the Four Heavenly Kings and appear in the palace of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."

At that time, the Buddha’s mother, Lady Māyā, having seen the Buddha’s alms bowl, was filled with grief and distress; it was as unbearable as an arrow piercing her heart. She rolled upon the ground like a log and spoke these words:
"How swift is the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa!"
How exceedingly swift is the passing of the Sugata!

The Eye of the World has been extinguished; the Buddha-tree has fallen, the Buddha-Sumeru has collapsed, and the Buddha-lamp has also gone out. The spring of the Dharma has run dry, and the sun of the Mara of Impermanence has withered the lotus-flower of the Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha’s mother, Lady Māyā, held the bowl with her hands and addressed all the devas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others, saying:
"Listen attentively, all you devas!"
This is the almsbowl constantly used by Śākyamuni Tathāgata; its reflection appears in this bowl, for his face is supremely courageous and perfectly full, surpassing the sun and moon.
Furthermore, O devas!
Furthermore, within the great city of Rājagṛha, this very bowl received poisoned food from Śrīgupta.
Listen attentively, O devas!
The Great Hero, the Muni Śākyamuni, ate his fill at the house of the Magadhan family in the city using this bowl.
"Listen attentively, all you devas!
In order to transform Uruvilvā-Kāśyapa and the great venomous dragon, the Tathāgata placed that evil dragon within this alms-bowl.
Listen attentively, all you devas!"
Due to the conditions of his karma, during the four months in the kingdom of Vairaṭya, he again received horse-barley in this very bowl.
Listen attentively, O assembly of devas!
Out of great compassion, Śākyamuni Tathāgata again received food from the most lowly and destitute of people with this very bowl.
Listen attentively, all you devas!
Śākyamuni Tathāgata again accepted various kinds of food in this bowl within the palace of the Naga King Sāgara.
Listen attentively, all you devas!
During the fourth month of the summer retreat, Śākyamuni Tathāgata again accepted our food with this very bowl.
Listen attentively, O devas!

With this same bowl, Śākyamuni Tathāgata covered the youngest son of the yakṣiṇī Hārītī, named Pilicula Yakṣa; because he possessed an evil mind and constantly consumed human blood, the Tathāgata subdued him.
Then the Buddha’s mother, Lady Māyā, received the bowl in her hands and spoke this verse:
"Whatever the Buddha’s heart desires to receive, All enters into this bowl;
Within my womb, the Buddha Was fulfilled for ten full months."

At that time, Śakra, King of the Devas, for seven days and seven nights, made extensive offerings with various celestial flowers, celestial incenses, and celestial sandalwood perfumes, prostrating and circumambulating him to the right.

Having made these offerings, among the assembly of devas, some resolved upon the unsurpassed mind of bodhi, some resolved upon the mind of a śrāvaka, and some resolved upon the mind of a pratyekabuddha.
At that time, the Heavenly King held the bowl with his hands and spoke these verses:
"This most excellent bowl Can increase the wisdom of sentient beings;
The Buddha’s body is likewise, Accomplishing all meritorious virtues."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"In this way, after seven days have passed, my almsbowl will vanish from the Heaven of the Thirty-three and reappear in the Yāma Heaven."

At that time, the Lord of the Yama Heaven, having beheld the Buddha’s bowl, made various offerings for seven days and seven nights. With celestial māndārava flowers, celestial sandalwood incense, diverse blossoms, and various kinds of music, he made offerings to the Buddha’s bowl, prostrating before it and circumambulating it to the right.

At that time, among the devas, some gave rise to the aspiration for unexcelled bodhi, some gave rise to the aspiration for the state of a śrāvaka, and some gave rise to the aspiration for the state of a pratyekabuddha.
Then, the Lord of the Yāma Heaven cupped his hands to receive the bowl and spoke these verses:
"Millions of billions of sentient beings, Upon seeing the bowl, all rejoice."
"Able to produce supreme and wondrous fruits, the Muni has sent me here.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"In this way, after seven days have passed, my bowl will vanish from the Yāma Heaven and appear in the Tuṣita Heaven."

At that time, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, having seen the Buddha’s bowl, for seven days and seven nights made a grand offering with celestial *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, and various other kinds of exquisite blossoms, incenses, and music. He prostrated, circumambulated it to the right, and holding the bowl in his hands, spoke these verses:
“For the sake of sentient beings of high, middling, and low station, The Buddha has given rise to a heart of compassion;
Having received food in this bowl, The Buddha has caused it to come here.”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"In this way, after seven days have passed, my bowl will vanish from Tuṣita Heaven and appear in Nirmāṇarati Heaven.

At that time, the King of Nirmāṇarati Heaven, having seen the Buddha’s bowl, will for seven days and seven nights provide a grand offering with various celestial flowers, various celestial incenses, and various celestial music, while prostrating and circumambulating it to the right."
At that time, among the host of devas, some gave rise to the unsurpassed mind of great bodhicitta, some gave rise to the mind of a śrāvaka, and some gave rise to the mind of a pratyekabuddha.
At that time, the Heavenly King cupped his hands to receive the bowl and spoke these verses:
"How rare is the Great Teacher, Who has compassion for all sentient beings!
For the sake of benefiting them, He has caused this bowl to come here."
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"At that time, the devas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, having made offerings to the bowl with celestial māndārava flowers, mahāmāndārava flowers, and various other kinds of flowers and incenses, including celestial sandalwood incense and powdered incense, immediately sent this bowl to the palace of the nāga king Sāgara."
The Buddha said,
“Ānanda! All the Buddha-bowls and the Buddha-relics throughout this Jambudvīpa and the other ten directions are all within the palace of the Dragon King Sāgara.”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"In this way, my almsbowl and my relics shall sink into this ground in a future age and pass directly through eighty thousand yojanas to rest upon the adamantine foundation."
Ānanda! I now tell you:

in a future age, when the lifespan of sentient beings is eighty-four thousand years, Maitreya Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—possessing the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, with a body the color of purple gold and a halo extending one fathom, and a voice like the drum of the Great Brahmā Heaven or the song of the kalaviṅka bird—will appear.

At that time, my alms bowl and my relics shall emerge from the adamantine base and arrive at the abode of Maitreya Buddha in Jambudvīpa; there, the bowl and the relics will remain suspended in mid-air, emitting five-colored rays of light—namely, blue, yellow, red, white, and variegated crystal colors.
Thus it was, Ānanda!
Those five-colored lights proceeded further to all other celestial realms; having reached those heavens, a voice issued from within the lights, reciting this verse:
"All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; All dharmas are without self."
"And the peace of nirvāṇa—these three are the seals of the Dharma.
The light then reached all the hells and spoke this verse:
"All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; all dharmas are without self."
"And the peace of Nirvāṇa—these three are the seals of the Dharma.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"The light emitted from the Buddha’s bowl and his relics further reached the worlds of the ten directions, and within that light, this verse was spoken:"
"All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; all dharmas are without self;
and the peace of nirvana—these three are the Dharma seals."
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“In this way, the radiance emitted by my almsbowl and my relics will perform the work of a Buddha throughout the worlds of the ten directions. Having done so, they will return to their original places and remain above the śarīra and the bowl in the midst of the sky, forming a great cloud-canopy of radiant light.”

Ānanda! When such rare and wondrous events as these—the appearance of the śarīra and the bowl—manifested, and when these miraculous and extraordinary feats were displayed, eight hundred billion sentient beings attained the fruit of arhatship; one thousand billion sentient beings shaved their heads and left the home life with pure faith; and ten thousand sentient beings gave rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, all of whom became non-retrogressive.
"Ānanda! After this bowl and these relics have extensively performed the work of teaching and transforming all sentient beings, they will remain suspended in the air before Maitreya.
At that time, the Buddha Maitreya, holding the bowl and the Buddha-relics in his hands, will address the devas, humans, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, saying:"
"You all should know!
This bowl and these relics are the result of the cultivation of faith, precepts, extensive learning, diligence, concentration, and wisdom by the Śākya-muni Tathāgata, the heroic and great being."

You should know this: the heroic and mighty Great Being Śākyamuni has enabled immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of sentient beings to dwell in the city of nirvāṇa; he has come here for the sake of the bowl and the śarīra relics, surpassing even the udumbara flower by hundreds of thousands of billions of times.

At that time, Maitreya Samyaksaṃbuddha shall erect a stūpa made of the four precious substances for this bowl of mine and for my relics, and he shall place the bowl containing the relics within this stūpa.

At that time, Maitreya Buddha, along with the devas, humans, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others, made grand offerings and paid reverent homage to the stūpa containing the śarīra relics.
The Buddha told Ānanda: “Ānanda,
the relics and the bowl of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, possess great majestic power.”
"By virtue of having served the physical body of the Tathāgata, the merit you have generated is immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable (asaṃkhyeya).
At that time, after the Buddha had explained these future matters to Ānanda, he further addressed Ānanda:
"I shall go with you to various lands; in no long time, seven days from now, the Tathāgata shall enter parinirvāṇa."
Ānanda replied to the Buddha, “So be it;
I shall receive your instruction.

At that time, the Buddha and Ānanda traveled in succession through various kingdoms and cities, delivering and liberating immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of sentient beings. They then proceeded to the home of the smith Cunda; this was the place where the Tathāgata would take his final meal.
At that time, having accepted his food, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"This is my final meal, Taken within the house of Cunda;
Such a body of the five aggregates Shall before long enter parinirvāṇa."

At that time, the Buddha and Ānanda went to the city of Kuśinagara; having used various skillful means to teach and transform the Mallas of Kuśinagara, they departed from the city and proceeded to the twin śāla trees at Upavartana.

At that time, the World-Honored One lay down with his head toward the north. Then Subhadra came to where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Tathāgata’s feet, and sat before him. The Buddha preached the Dharma for him, and he attained the fruit of Arhatship.
The Sūtra of the Lotus-Faced One, Scroll II.
